name: Hive Backed Dollar
oneLiner: HBD is Hive's algorithmic dollar, redeemable on-chain for $1 of HIVE via a witness-set conversion, with haircut rules when system debt exceeds thresholds.
collateral: Hive protocol value and conversion rules between HBD and HIVE, including haircut logic when HBD debt exceeds protocol thresholds
pegMechanism: Protocol-level conversion mechanism targets one U.S. dollar of HIVE per HBD, with witness-set interest and haircut rules under stress

oracleRisk.summary: Hive derives the HIVE/HBD conversion price from fresh scheduled-witness submissions, takes their median, and then takes the median over a 3.5-day history window; protocol-wide debt caps can constrain the effective conversion price and HBD issuance.

branchApplicability.rationale: HBD is protocol-level debt backed by the value of HIVE and converted under one consensus-wide price-feed and debt-ratio rule set. Holders do not open borrower-specific collateral positions, and Hive exposes no separately liquidatable collateral markets requiring branch rows.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: reviewed metadata or audit notes identify direct seizure, freeze, blacklist, privileged burn, proxy-upgrade, or chain-governance intervention authority despite decentralized governance labeling.

sources.label: Hive glossary (HBD conversion and haircut mechanics)

reserveReview.rationale: HBD is a native Hive protocol liability, not a claim on a segregated reserve portfolio: there are no asset reserves, only the protocol's conversion rule paying $1 of HIVE per HBD at the 3.5-day median witness price, bounded by the debt-ratio haircut. Live chain properties at 2026-07-19 report about 32.4M HBD outstanding with the DHF account itself holding roughly 72% of supply, and the community HBD stabilizer bot is inactive, so peg defense rests on conversions, the haircut, and the witness-set savings rate.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Hive protocol conversion and haircut mechanism confirmed against live chain properties
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: There is no external reserve custodian, asset allocation, or legally segregated collateral pool. HBD holders instead depend on Hive protocol value, witness-set price submissions, and the protocol debt-limit and haircut rules; whether the protocol's debt-ratio accounting nets out DHF-held HBD is not definitively documented in the reviewed sources.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: Backing is the Hive protocol's own conversion capacity denominated in HIVE market value — a self-referential protocol reserve rather than an exogenous asset or tracked stablecoin.

providers.name: Hive base-layer protocol (conversion mechanism; no reserve custodian)

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-2 (lead buidl-blackrock)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: HBD has no reserve assets to custody: backing is the protocol-native conversion rule against HIVE market value. Custody concepts (segregation, bankruptcy remoteness, rehypothecation) do not apply; the operative risks are witness price-feed integrity, the 3.5-day conversion delay, and the debt-ratio haircut degrading the $1 conversion rate when protocol debt is high.

notices.title: Protocol haircut mechanism
notices.message: HBD redemptions depend on Hive protocol conversion rules and can be haircut when system debt is above configured thresholds.

notices.title: Hive-native asset
notices.message: HBD is issued by the Hive protocol rather than an EVM-style token contract. Pharos does not list a contract address until Hive is supported in the chain metadata registry.

mintAuthority.summary: HBD is created at the Hive protocol layer through a HIVE<->HBD conversion mechanism; supply expands when HIVE is converted to HBD, bounded by a debt-ratio cap (printing halts at 20% of virtual supply; haircut kicks in at 30%) and the witness consensus set tunes these parameters. Confirmed from live chain state: hbd_start_percent=2000, hbd_stop_percent=2000, HIVE_HBD_HARD_LIMIT=3000, current hbd_print_rate=0 (printing halted at ~53% debt ratio).

controls.label: Hive conversion mechanism (protocol-level mint/burn)
controls.capDescription: HBD is minted via on-chain HIVE->HBD conversion (3.5-day time-averaged HIVE price); debt-ratio cap halts printing at 20% of virtual supply (hbd_start_percent/stop_percent=2000); haircut on HIVE→HBD conversions kicks in at 30% of HIVE market cap (HIVE_HBD_HARD_LIMIT=3000). Current hbd_print_rate=0 (minting halted).
controls.evidence: Hive blockchain API (database_api.get_config) confirmed: hbd_start_percent=2000, hbd_stop_percent=2000, HIVE_HBD_HARD_LIMIT=3000. get_dynamic_global_properties confirmed: hbd_print_rate=0 (printing fully halted), current_hbd_supply≈32.9M HBD, virtual_supply≈1.24B HIVE (~$61.9M at $0.05). HBD debt ratio ≈53% >> 20% start threshold; printing stopped. No permissioned minter: conversion is enforced by Hive consensus code open to all users.

controls.label: Hive witness consensus set (parameter governance)
controls.evidence: Block-producing witnesses set HBD interest/savings APR (currently 12% — hbd_interest_rate=1200) and can soft-fork the debt-limit parameters (hbd_start_percent, hbd_stop_percent) via consensus. HIVE_HBD_HARD_LIMIT=3000 is a hard-coded constant requiring a chain hard fork to change. Witnesses tune issuance terms but do not directly mint to arbitrary accounts.

review.evidence: Hive blockchain API (database_api.get_config and get_dynamic_global_properties) confirmed live consensus parameters: hbd_start_percent=2000 (HBD printing halted at 20% of virtual_supply), hbd_stop_percent=2000 (printing resumes below 20%), HIVE_HBD_HARD_LIMIT=3000 (30% debt ratio triggers haircut on HIVE→HBD conversions). Current state: hbd_print_rate=0 (printing fully halted; current HBD supply ~32.9M at ~53% of virtual_supply ~1.24B HIVE). HBD interest rate is 1200 (12% APR), set by witness consensus. These are all witness-tunable soft-fork parameters.
